diagnostics.message: :data.http.wait_for_cluster: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_eks_cluster.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`data.http.wait_for_cluster` declares `depends_on = [aws_eks_cluster.this, ...]`, but `aws_eks_cluster.this` is already referenced implicitly by the data source's own arguments (`url = format("%s/healthz", aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint)` and `ca_certificate = base64decode(...aws_eks_cluster.this[*]...)`). The `aws_eks_cluster.this` entry in that `depends_on` list duplicates the ordering Terraform already infers, so it can be dropped (only `aws_security_group_rule.cluster_private_access` is a genuine non-attribute ordering requirement).

`module.fargate:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this` is created with a freshly created pod execution role (`pod_execution_role_arn = local.pod_execution_role_arn` -> `aws_iam_role.eks_fargate_pod`), so ordering against the role itself is inferred, but nothing orders it after `module.fargate:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eks_fargate_pod`. EKS validates/uses the pod execution role when the profile is created, and a role that was just created and has no policy attachment yet can hit IAM propagation problems (and pods scheduled through the profile get no ECR/CloudWatch permissions). The existing `eks_depends_on` hack only carries the cluster and the aws-auth ConfigMap; the role policy attachment should be added to that list (or a direct `depends_on` added on the profile).
